messages:
alex: Pager: high throttle events and degraded tail latency on private-prod-gpu cluster. Seeing lots of 429s from inference runtime. Paging on-call now.

samir: looking. getting stack traces and qdepth metrics. suspect autoscaler didn't add nodes. saw a spike at ~11:03 UTC.

jules: confirmed token/sec dropped ~60% and queue_depth spiked to 2200 on queue 'inference-east-1'. normal is ~200-400.

maria: @alex any customer-impact? we already got a support ticket from ACME corp reporting timeouts.

alex: ACME calls show requests timing out at ~30s. Not full cluster outage but severe degradation for heavy prompt workloads.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0032 - Capacity saturation / autoscaler lag. Severity: P1. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/capacity-saturation

samir: preliminary check: autoscale controller logs show repeated "scale rejected: target tokens/sec below min_threshold" errors. looks like a config drift: min_tokens_per_node set to 8000 but observed token/sec per node is ~7000 due to longer contexts. controller refused to add nodes.

jules: that explains it. we should override to allow burst capacity.

alex: I can flip emergency burst flag. Doing: `kubectl annotate deployment autoscaler emergency=true --namespace=infra`

autoscale-bot: Emergency burst enabled by alex at 11:06 UTC. Spinning up 4 nodes (requested). Estimated ready in ~2-4m.

maria: also clearing prefix cache for the hottest customer to reduce KV pressure — running:
```
curl -XPOST https://internal-cache/evict -d '{"namespace":"acme","prefix":"session:"}'
```

samir: nodes are starting. seeing new GPU nodes join at 11:09. queue_depth dropping from 2200 -> 900 -> 300. tail latency improving.

jules: throttle events reduced, 429s dropped by 90% per log tail. ACME support report updated: partial recovery.

alex: I'm going to temporarily raise queue_depth alert threshold to avoid noisy paging while autoscaler stabilizes. Changing alert `qdepth-high` from 500 -> 2000. (will revert after postmortem).

maria: please add a note in the incident about alert change and reason.

samir: logged in Ops timeline: adjusted min_tokens_per_node to 6000 to reflect longer context usage and prevent reject loops.

alex: Confirmed: autoscaler accepted new target. New scale policy will be pushed to infra-config repo after incident.

incident-bot: Timeline updated.

jules: quick mitigation checklist: emergency burst enabled, prefix cache cleared, min_tokens_per_node temporarily lowered, queue_depth alert relaxed. Customer impact reduced.

maria: can we add a short-term dashboard tile for tokens/sec per node + rolling 10m median to detect this earlier? current dashboard is 1m granularity and noisy.

samir: good idea. I'll add a panel: `tokens/sec per node (10m median)`, and another for `autoscaler-rejections` count.

alex: also consider adding a guard in autoscaler to avoid hard rejects: if recent cluster utilization > 80% for >2m, prefer to scale up even if per-node token estimate slightly below min.

jules: agree. filing a GH issue: infra/autoscaler#458 with proposal and config diff.

maria: post-incident action items: 1) revert queue_depth alert back to 500 after validation 2) add dashboard panels 3) update autoscale policy and add a canary test for long-context workloads 4) docs entry for emergency-burst annotation 5) notify affected customers with SLA note.

alex: I'll handle #1 and #5. samir take #2 and #3. jules take #4 and the GH issue.

samir: starting on the dashboard now, will push a temporary Grafana at https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd123/capacity-surge (will make permanent after review).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0032 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned owners for follow-ups.

maria: recommend a postmortem with impact table (affected customer list, duration, tokens lost) and include suggested SLA credits if needed.

jules: noted. I'll prepare the postmortem draft and link configs.

alex: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread as the single source for the mitigation timeline and action owners. If anyone sees remaining anomalies, ping here. :thumbsup:
